A1.justification: Both PDFs are complete, readable versions of the same MDGFM study. Their text, equations, tables, figures and appendices support reliable comparison, including material relocated or relettered in v2.

before.justification: v1 reports original few-shot node-classification experiments, component ablations, source-domain sensitivity tests and robustness analyses, including appendix results.

after.justification: v2 retains the study's original classification, ablation, sensitivity and robustness results in the main text and appendices.

M1.justification: Sections 4.1–4.3 and the matching methodology and loss appendices retain the same feature projection, tokens, graph refinement, contrastive objective and dual-prompt adaptation. The new complexity appendix analyzes the existing procedure.

E1.justification: Both versions evaluate few-shot node classification on Cora, Citeseer, Pubmed, Cornell, Squirrel, Chameleon and Penn94. The represented domains and robustness scenarios are unchanged.

E2.justification: The evaluated comparator sets are unchanged. Table 4 relabels MDGPT as SAMGPT, with identical scores; both versions associate MDGPT with Yu et al. (2025), whose reference already names SAMGPT.

E3.justification: Source/target assignments, shot counts, attack procedures and model settings are retained. Tables 7–8 and v1 Appendix D/v2 Appendix E give the same backbone configuration, feature dimensions, learning rates, epochs and graph-construction settings.

E4.justification: Both versions contain the same four component ablations, source-domain removal study, edge-addition/deletion and Metattack tests, and k sensitivity analysis (Figures 2–5; Table 4). The additional-experiment appendix moves from C to D without new experimental analyses.

E5.justification: Both report five experimental runs, 50 downstream resampling iterations and the same mean-accuracy-plus-standard-deviation reporting. Uncertainty displays in the figures are also retained.

E6.justification: Numerical results in Tables 1–4 and plotted findings in Figures 2–5 are unchanged. For example, MDGFM's Cora one-shot accuracy remains 44.83 ± 7.41, and its Penn94 accuracy at K=500 remains 63.25 ± 0.82. No measured runtime results are added.

T1.justification: New Appendix B derives component-wise and total asymptotic costs for pre-training and downstream adaptation, extending v1's existing kNN complexity discussion. The domain-generalization theorems, invariance assumption and existing mathematical formulations remain unchanged.

C1.justification: The abstract, introduction and conclusion retain the same claims about topology alignment, robust cross-domain transfer, theoretical guarantees and novelty across homophilic and heterophilic domains. Minor wording additions do not alter their scientific scope.

C2.justification: Appendix B newly concludes that the overall model scales linearly with node and edge counts, attributing this to efficient structure refinement and modular design. This extends v1's narrower kNN efficiency explanation; interpretations of the empirical results remain unchanged.

D1.justification: v2 adds a code-repository link in the abstract and identifies the PCA operation as truncated PCA in Appendix B. These add access information and implementation specificity; the existing hardware, software, optimizer and hyperparameter disclosures are retained.

R1.justification: v2 adds seven references, including GFT, PC-CONV and attribute-driven graph domain adaptation, principally supporting existing introductory and related-work statements. The central research positioning remains unchanged; publication updates to existing references do not introduce different works.

P1.justification: v2 inserts a complexity appendix, reletters subsequent appendices, adds an impact statement and acknowledgments, and updates author contribution and publication information. Local wording and naming edits occur, but most prose and the main narrative structure are retained.

P2.justification: Existing displays are retained with limited relocation and reflow: Figure 1 moves from page 3 to 4, Figure 4 from page 13 to 14, and Table 7 from page 14 to 15. Table 4 changes a comparator header; the plotted graphics, axes and underlying table structures remain unchanged.

improvement.justification: The repository pointer and new computational discussion modestly improve reproducibility information and documentation while preserving the existing empirical evidence. The gain is limited: Appendix B does not explicitly account for the contrastive-loss calculations in Equations 14–15, leaving its claimed total linear scaling incompletely supported.
